 Why ‘Wildwood’s PG-13 Rating Signals a Major Shift for Animated Movies
 Paulina Colosio 
 Staff Writer · October 24, 2026 · 7 min read 
 Follow 
 Table of Contents A PG-13 Is a Warning, Not a Wall 
 Animation’s PG-13 Shelf Is Short and Mostly Full of Warnings 
 The Ceiling Broke Somewhere Else First 
 The PG Audience Still Pays for Everything 
 What the Rating Buys and What It Costs 
 Laika’s Clock Runs Longer Than Opening Weekend 
 “Strong fantasy violence/bloody images, thematic material, suicide related material, brief partial nudity and language.” That is the Motion Picture Association’s descriptor for Wildwood , and Dark Horizons reported the full string in August. Six features into a 17-year run, Laika has made a movie the ratings board would not wave through as a family picture.
 The rest of the spec sheet reads the same way. The film runs 132 minutes, the longest stop-motion feature ever released, past the 117-minute mark Guinness World Records handed Guillermo del Toro’s Pinocchio in 2022. Travis Knight directed from a script by Chris Butler , working from the 2011 novel Carson Ellis illustrated and Colin Meloy wrote, with Peyton Elizabeth Lee voicing Prue. Knight has walked through the 16-year production in detail, and the cast and the source material are laid out in our Wildwood breakdown . The build came to 231 puppets across 136 sets. Fathom Entertainment opens it nationwide on October 23.
 The Wildwood PG-13 rating does one concrete, measurable thing. It narrows the door. Theatrical animation runs on the under-13 ticket bought by an adult who buys a second ticket for themselves at the same counter, and a PG-13 tells that adult to stop and consider. Every other question about this film, awards included, sits downstream of that one.
 Wildwood / Credits: Laika 
 A PG-13 Is a Warning, Not a Wall
 Nothing about the label keeps a child out of the auditorium. PG-13 is advisory, so a ten-year-old can buy a ticket and sit down unaccompanied, which is the detail that disappears every time a studio takes one. The restriction is social, not legal. A parent reads the descriptor, finds the phrases “suicide related material” and “bloody images” attached to a stop-motion story about a girl and her stolen baby brother, and picks the other movie on the marquee. That choice gets made in a parking lot, and no review score reaches it.
 Laika’s first five features all went out with a PG, including Coraline and Kubo and the Two Strings , and neither one is a gentle film. Kubo spends its last act on a child bargaining with the dead and still carried the family label. The content had been drifting toward this rating for a decade before the board finally wrote it down. What shifted in August was the paperwork catching up to what Laika has been making since 2009.
 Animation’s PG-13 Shelf Is Short and Mostly Full of Warnings
 The precedent is thin enough to list. Beavis and Butt-Head Do America took a PG-13 in 1996 for crude humor and a drug-related scene, cost Paramount $12 million, and finished with $63.1 million domestic, according to The Numbers . It worked because the budget was a rounding error and MTV had pre-sold the audience years in advance.
 Five years later Columbia tried the same rating with real money behind it. Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within carried a PG-13 for sci-fi action violence, a $137 million budget, and a worldwide gross of $85.1 million. Square Pictures closed in January 2002. The lesson the industry drew had more to do with photorealism than with content descriptors, but the rating is part of why nobody in the family-film business wanted to run that experiment again.
 The counterexample is more recent and more useful. The Boy and the Heron went out through GKIDS with a PG-13 in December 2023, finished with $47.3 million domestic and $275.1 million worldwide per Box Office Mojo , and then won the Academy Award. A PG-13 animated film can travel and it can win. The budget underneath it has to be one a specialty release can actually carry.
 The Ceiling Broke Somewhere Else First
 Adult-facing animation already proved it can open huge, and no American studio had to be brave for that to happen. Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle opened to $70.6 million domestic in September 2025 on an R rating for bloody violence throughout, the largest opening ever recorded for an R-rated animated film, as The A.V. Club laid out. Cartoon Brew later put its worldwide total above $555 million.
 That figure comes with an asterisk the size of a building. Demon Slayer arrived with a decade of manga and a hit series pre-selling every seat, which is a very different proposition from asking a general audience to commit two hours to handmade puppets they have never met. The honest seasonal comparison is Ray Gunn , and it runs the other way. Brad Bird’s Skydance Animation detective picture stars Sam Rockwell as a private eye in an alternate 1939, cost a reported $150 million or more, and took a PG for violence, action, language, some suggestive material and thematic elements. It reaches Netflix on December 18 after a limited theatrical run beginning December 4.
 Bird’s film is the more adult object by temperament and it wears the softer label, which tells you the Wildwood PG-13 rating was a decision Laika made rather than a verdict forced on it. Skydance had $150 million riding on it and a streamer waiting underneath, and it trimmed to PG. Laika had a smaller number, a specialty distributor and no safety net, and it went the other way.
 Hoppers / Photo Credit: Disney, Pixar 
 The PG Audience Still Pays for Everything
 Pixar spent 2026 demonstrating what a rating is worth in cash. Hoppers opened to $46 million domestic back in March, which was the strongest Pixar-original debut since Coco landed in 2017, Deadline reported, and Cartoon Brew later clocked its lifetime global gross at $375.1 million using figures from The Numbers. It is rated PG. It is also about a college student who moves her consciousness into the body of a robotic beaver to stop a land developer, a premise stranger than anything in Prue’s forest, and six-year-olds showed up for it anyway.
 A PG guarantees nothing on its own. Forgotten Island , the DreamWorks feature Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado built around Philippine folklore and a friendship one of the girls trades away to a memory-stealing spirit, cost $80 million and has taken roughly $46 million worldwide since its September 25 release. Ambition inside a family rating is no safe harbor. The rating sets the size of the room, and what you put in the room still has to work.
 Forgotten Island / Photo courtesy of Universal 
 What the Rating Buys and What It Costs
 Laika’s Wildwood PG-13 rating bought critical cover the studio has already cashed. Rotten Tomatoes has the film at 100% across 66 reviews with a 98% audience score, the best set of numbers Laika has ever opened with. For a company carrying five Best Animated Feature nominations and zero wins, from Coraline through Missing Link , that is worth more than usual. The one trophy on the shelf is the 2020 Golden Globe Missing Link took over Disney’s slate, and The Boy and the Heron settled the question of whether a PG-13 blocks an Academy win.
 The cost arrives this weekend. Boxoffice Pro trimmed its long-range domestic forecast to a $6 million to $10 million opening, down from $10 million to $15 million a week earlier, against a budget widely reported near $100 million that Laika has never confirmed. Fathom Entertainment is a specialty exhibitor rather than a wide-release machine, a 132-minute runtime cuts the number of daily showtimes a screen can hold, and Clayface is absorbing most of the weekend’s wide-release attention.
 Wildwood / Credits: Laika 
 Laika’s Clock Runs Longer Than Opening Weekend
 Laika’s own catalog makes the longer argument. The studio’s 15th-anniversary Coraline re-release has out-earned Missing Link ‘s entire domestic run, $33.6 million against $16.6 million, per Box Office Mojo . Nothing Laika makes finishes earning on schedule. The opening weekend is a down payment, and the asset keeps paying out in anniversary screenings and remasters for a decade and a half.
 The runtime is a separate gamble from the rating, and the two compound. At 132 minutes Wildwood sits eight minutes under Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse , the longest animated feature a Hollywood studio has ever put in theaters. That film had Sony’s marketing and a Spider-Man on the poster. Laika has a girl, a forest and a murder of crows, and it is asking exhibitors to surrender a screen for four showings a day where a 95-minute cartoon would have delivered six. Fathom took the booking anyway, which is a more interesting vote of confidence than any studio statement.
 My read is that the Wildwood PG-13 rating will look like the cheapest line on this ledger once the film is done earning. Laika took its riskiest swing to the ratings board, accepted the most restrictive label in company history, collected the best reviews of its life for the trouble, and walked into the weekend with an opening forecast smaller than the number of puppets on its shelves. Prue’s rescue mission takes 132 minutes to finish. Laika’s runs on a fifteen-year clock, the one Coraline has been quietly winning since 2009.

 About the author 
 Paulina Colosio 
 Staff Writer 
 Paulina Colosio, though everyone calls her Pau, is a marketing professional, film enthusiast, and creative storyteller with a Bachelor of Arts in Marketing and Communications from Tecnológico de Monterrey, where she earned multiple academic recognitions for excellence throughout her program. 
 During her time there, she interned at the campus radio station, Azul 83, developing and producing several projects such as podcasts and radio programs that explored campus life and her personal interests, particularly British music. After graduating, Paulina co-founded BluHart Stories in 2023, an independent film production company born out of her desire to continue collaborating with her university friends to share their passion for creating audiovisual art and Mexican culture with the rest of the world. 
 As Executive Producer and Co-Founder, she has played a key role in bringing a variety of artistic projects to life, including two award-winning short films, “La Tragedia de un Momento” and “Nadie Será Tú”, which were selected for multiple international film festivals, the web series “Señor Frijol,” and several music videos for local artists.
